newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-TIP FROM UNCLE GERMAN HELPS GARRIDO TO FIRST ROUND LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIP FROM UNCLE GERMAN HELPS GARRIDO TO FIRST ROUND LEAD.

text.p: A tip from his uncle German, a former European Tour pro, helped Ignacio Garrido to a two-stroke lead at the halfway stage of the German Open on Friday.
The advice came before the final round of his victory in last week's Spanish PGA, a non-European Tour event.
"My uncle noticed I was using my hands too much which meant I kept hooking and pulling when I am a natural fader of the ball," said Garrido.
"I felt much happier after adjusting my swing and that helped me shoot a 68 in the wind in Madrid and I won by three."

The young Spaniard, who is seeking to go one better than three second place finishes he has had since joining the Tour in 1994, climaxed his four-under-par 67 by rattling in a 30-foot birdie up over a ridge.
He led by two shots on 132 from Argentine Eduardo Romero who birdied five of his first six holes.
Romero closed to within one shot of Garrido with three holes to play but then bunkered himself twice for bogeys at the 16th and 17th. He birdied the last.
Englishman Mark James, 43, had his first tournament round hole in one of a 20-year career when he aced the 194-yard eighth, his 17th hole, with a five iron. A 67 left him three off the pace.
"It's amazing that this is my first hole in one in a tournament but that perhaps shows how bad my iron play has been over the years," he joked.
James lies 21st in the European Ryder Cup table but dismissed suggestions of an eighth team place if he wins in Stuttgart.
"I'd need to win this week and earn another 100,000 points and that may be too much," he said.
